rawFindings.title: Case-sensitive route deduping breaks `app.all()` reuse for non-string paths when router is case-sensitive
rawFindings.explanation: `_baseRoute()` now indexes routes by lowercasing the path whenever `this._router.caseSensitive` is false, but it still uses `path.ignoreCase` without first ensuring `path` is a string-like route object. If a non-string path object is passed to `app.all()`/`app.VERB()` in a case-sensitive app, the new cache key logic can collapse distinct route objects with different case-sensitivity flags into the same cached route, so later handlers are attached to the wrong route instance.
rawFindings.suggestion: Only derive the cache key from `ignoreCase` when `path` is a route object, and include the route object's own case-sensitivity in the cache key; otherwise skip the lowercase normalization for non-string paths.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Calling `app.all({ path: '/Users', ignoreCase: false }, fn1)` and then `app.all({ path: '/users', ignoreCase: true }, fn2)` in the same app can attach both handlers to the same cached route, so requests match the wrong handler ordering/case behavior.
